project.title: Mind the Gap — the project
project.desc: Where Mind the Gap stands, the plan to make it a working service, the decks for investors and institutions, and how to help.
project.heroTitle: From a prototype to a working service, in four phases.
project.heroLede: Mind the Gap is one index for the art world: commissions, residencies and the institutions behind them, each checked against its source. This page holds the plan, the two decks and the ways to help, in one place.
project.docsTitle: The plan, and the two decks.
project.docsNote: Documents open in a new tab.
project.nowTitle: A working prototype on real data. Nobody can sign up yet.
project.nowLede: {L} listings and {P} institutions in {K} countries, shown through an intro, a world index and {E} editions. Each listing links to the page it was checked against, but only {H} of the {L} are rated high confidence. The first job is to check every one at its source.
project.confTitle: How sure we are of the {L} listings
project.roadmapTitle: Four phases. Each ends at a gate, and the next starts only when the gate is met.
project.roadmapLede: Each phase pairs what gets built with the work on the ground: editors who check listings at their source, institutions that keep their own listings right, and the artists and collectors who use the index. Software makes that faster but cannot replace it, because a wrong deadline costs an artist a year.
project.timelineLabel: The 30 months of the plan, by phase
project.timelineNow: Now: the prototype. Phase 0 starts once it is funded.
project.budgetLine: A first estimate: $3.97 million over 30 months, or $4.57 million with a 15% reserve, employer costs included.

phases.name: Foundations
phases.summary: Make the data trustworthy enough to put in front of people.
phases.team: Founder, tech lead, editor-in-chief, two researchers, a half-time product designer

gate.what: Pilot listings checked on their source pages, standards published, founding partners signed, the name cleared, the company and its policies in place.
gate.target: 100% of Israel and US listings verified; 20 institutions signed in each pilot market; no open legal blocker

phases.name: Pilot
phases.summary: The first time artists and institutions use Mind the Gap, in Israel and New York.
phases.team: Adds a full-stack engineer, a partnerships lead, and a community and events lead

gate.what: Artists sign up and come back, institutions keep their own listings right, and mistakes are fixed fast.
gate.target: 5,000 artist accounts; 40% open an alert each month; 60 institutions manage their listings; 95% of reported mistakes fixed within 48 hours

phases.name: Six regions
phases.summary: Every region kept current by an editor who reads its languages, and institutions start to pay.
phases.team: Adds a second engineer, six half-time regional editors, and institution sales

gate.what: Editors keep six regions current, and institutions pay.
gate.target: 1,000 verified listings; 90% re-checked before their cycle opens; 50 paying institutions

phases.name: Collector layer
phases.summary: Collectors meet artists through the index, and any money moves through a licensed partner.
phases.team: Adds a third engineer, a collector lead, and half-time compliance

gate.what: Collectors use the index to meet artists; any money moves through a licensed partner.
gate.target: 500 collector members; 200 studio visits arranged; compliance approved by counsel

built.name: Data platform
built.what: One database for organisations, programmes, calls, places and people. Every fact keeps its source page, a saved copy, the date checked, who checked it and how.

built.name: Editorial tools
built.what: A queue where editors verify, correct and publish, with reminders to re-check before each cycle and alerts when an organiser’s page changes. AI drafts fields from a page and quotes the line it used; an editor confirms each one.

built.name: Public site
built.what: The intro, world index and editions rebuilt as one app, so every call has its own page that search engines can find.

built.name: Accessibility and speed
built.what: WCAG 2.2 AA, fast on a phone and readable with scripting off, as the prototype already is.

built.name: Artist accounts
built.what: Sign-up, an eligibility profile, saved calls, weekly email alerts, a calendar feed and “report a mistake”.

built.name: Eligibility matching
built.what: Each call’s rules stored as fields rather than prose, so the site answers “can you apply?” for each artist and says why not.

built.name: Institution accounts
built.what: Verified organisation accounts that claim listings, correct them, post calls and see how many artists viewed and saved them.

built.name: Trust and safety
built.what: Flags for entry fees and pay-to-exhibit calls, a correction log on every listing, and review of what institutions post.

built.name: Languages
built.what: Every edition in its own language, right to left where needed. Listings machine-translated, then approved by an editor.

built.name: Open data
built.what: A public feed of verified listings for partners and researchers, under an open licence with attribution.

built.name: Paid tools for institutions
built.what: Call pages, shortlists, links into the submission systems they already use, and reports for their funders.

built.name: Collector layer
built.what: Collector accounts, follows, studio-visit requests and records of each work held by the artist. Payments only through a licensed partner, after anti-money-laundering checks.

ground.name: Re-verification
ground.what: Open the source page of every listing and institution. Confirm or correct each one, add the deadline where the organiser publishes one, and retire what has closed.

ground.name: Editorial standards
ground.what: Write the rules: what counts as a source, how confidence is rated, how fast a reported mistake is fixed, and when each listing is re-checked.

ground.name: Founding institutions
ground.what: Sign 20 to 30 institutions in each pilot market that confirm their own listings every cycle, in return for a verified badge and reach.

ground.name: Artists in the pilot
ground.what: Work through art schools and artists’ associations in both cities, hold a monthly application clinic, and interview 30 artists before building accounts.

ground.name: Company and legal
ground.what: Incorporate, assign the work to the company, and write terms, a privacy policy and data agreements with partners.

ground.name: Name and brand
ground.what: Clear the name for the services it covers, and choose a fallback.

ground.name: Funding
ground.what: Fund Phases 0 and 1 from investors, grants from arts foundations and public cultural funds, and supporters.

ground.name: Networks and data partners
ground.what: Agree data sharing, both ways, with residency networks and national arts councils.

ground.name: Regional editors
ground.what: One editor per region who reads its main languages, paid a retainer plus a fee per verified listing, and trained on the standards.

ground.name: Collectors
ground.what: Small collector circles through museum patron groups and fairs in the pilot cities, with studio visits. Learn what collectors would pay for before building payments.

ground.name: Money and compliance
ground.what: Take advice before any payment between collector and artist, which brings anti-money-laundering duties.

support.heroTitle: Help us check every listing at its source.
support.heroLede: Mind the Gap puts commissions, residencies and the institutions behind them in one free index, and artists never pay to find a call. Before anyone relies on it, each of its {L} listings and {P} institutions has to be opened at its source, confirmed or corrected, and dated. That takes people, and it is the first thing your support pays for.
support.goalBody: Three months of an editor and two researchers, checking every listing.

support.donateNote: Donations are taken on GoFundMe. A donation is a gift, not an investment.
support.whyTitle: Only {H} of {L} listings are rated high confidence.
support.whyBody: A wrong deadline costs an artist a year, so nothing else is built on the listings until each one has been checked by a person at its source. {UL} of them were read only through search excerpts, without opening the page. About one commission in four, {INV} of {CC}, takes no applications at all, which is exactly what an artist needs to know before spending a week on a proposal.

faq.a: No. A donation is a gift: it buys no share in Mind the Gap and is not paid back. GoFundMe takes donations only.
No. Mind the Gap is not yet a company or a registered charity, so a donation is a personal gift to the organiser, not a tax-deductible donation.

There is no platform fee. A payment-processing fee comes off each donation: in the US it is 2.9% plus 30 cents, and rates differ by country. GoFundMe also asks donors for an optional tip, which goes to GoFundMe, not to us, and can be set to zero.

faq.q: What if the goal is not reached?
faq.a: Everything raised is still spent in the order above: the re-check comes first, starting with the listings in Israel and the United States, where the pilot opens.

faq.q: How will I know what it paid for?
faq.a: We post an update on the campaign at each step: what was checked, what changed and what it cost. Once the database is built, every listing shows the date it was checked.

faq.q: Can I help in another way?
faq.a: Yes. Artists can tell us what is wrong or missing, institutions can become founding partners, and anyone can share the index with an artist who needs it. The project page has the details.
